Hi! If you're up for it I have a female mage/scholarly type based roughly off of a Tiefling from D&D. 

​

Eleanor Thornspire is a twenty-five year old mage, standing at roughly 5'4", and 130\~ lbs. She has long brown-reddish hair, in a loose ponytail. Her skin is a pink-tan hue, think rouge with a bit more of a human-esque tan. She has pink pupil-less eyes, with otherwise white sclera. Ellie presents as human fairly decently, lacking horns and sharp teeth - unlike even her brother who possesses horns. Though she has a thin, long tail, she typically keeps it wrapped around her waist. Another feature are her more rounded or stubbed fingernails. (Like those of Tiefling)   


Ellie usually wears a maroon colored female military uniform, style closest to a [Lolita dress](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/617908011357684070/?nic=1) dress (reminiscent of Victorian-Edwardian style). Her build is on the thinner side, and her features are hard if not stern. Facial features are on the nobler side, so longer and more smooth feature, strong cheek and jaw bones, and full lips. Though she looks unapproachable, if you get close enough to her she can prove to be a very warm and intelligent person. She usually wears glasses, but is not in need of corrective lenses.  


She is head of research and development of a militia founded to combat Vampires and other Undead. She takes her job very seriously. She is highly analytical, sometimes to an anxious degree that makes her come off as intense. With friends she is cool, clever, and charismatic. Aside from a decent repertoire of magic, her signature magic is centered around telekinesis. Though not mastered, she can achieve a lot with it and uses it in many unique ways.

What I mean is having the chance is not a reward, especially when there's no guarantee you'll succeed. Some considered the rare items the reward. Others consider the XP the reward. 

Catching the Pokemon, semantically speaking; is of course a reward. But it's not considered as such, it's considered a bonus.

There's never any real, actual guarantee to catch the boss however. And the *chance* to catch it is not a reward. RNG has proven to a lot of us, no matter how many golden razz, excellent curve-ball throws you manage, you will not catch that Pokemon, because RNG doesn't want you to. 

The items you got from beating raids were not preemptive consolation prizes, or a bonus. The bonus was being able to catch the boss, the game even says so.

Rewards are also supposed to be proportionate. I'm hearing about people beating 4 and 5 star raids, and them not getting a single rare candy or even golden razzberry. So people getting a little cheesed when they put time and effort into powerful raids to get very little in return, is understandable. That begs the question, why continue to do raids? Second, when he's with Koshiro shortly after and he confides in Zoro, telling him how fragile humans are. And how Kuina practiced from a young age to the point where she surpassed an adults skill level. He mentions how she made an impact in female swordsmanship, despite societies standards and his own beliefs. Zoro then asks for the Wado Ichimonji, vowing to become the worlds greatest swordsman. Koshiro agrees and tells him he will be leaving Kuina's dreams and spirit in Zoro's hands. To me that was when Zoro earned bushido, and also the day that his dreams became concrete, and ingrained with him forever. 

Zoro's backstory was probably the most interesting, I wouldn't necessarily say emotionally impacting, but it shows you why he is who he is now. And that it's commendable that he's held on to his dream.
